findings.comment: `h.container` is a shared singleton accessed concurrently across all incoming HTTP requests. Overwriting `h.container.Logger` per request and restoring it in `defer` causes a severe race condition: concurrent requests will overwrite each other's logger, mix up request contexts/trace IDs, and restore `origLogger` prematurely while another request is still processing.

Allocating a map[string]any on every log call introduces heap allocations and GC overhead on the logging path. In addition, using a map with the string key "__trace_id__" relies on magic strings and could potentially collide with user-provided map data.

extractTraceIDAndFilterArgs allocates a new slice on every single log call even when no trace ID is present in args. For the majority of log calls where no trace ID is injected (such as background tasks, startup, or when tracing is disabled), allocating and copying arguments into filtered adds unnecessary heap allocations to the logging hot path.

Using a generic map[string]any with a magic key "__trace_id__" to pass metadata between ContextLogger and logger requires allocating a map on every traced log statement, and risks stripping user data if user code logs a map containing "__trace_id__" with other fields. Because both ContextLogger and logger reside in package logging, an unexported type (such as type traceID string) can be used instead.
